newsitem.title: GERMANY: Wall Street cheer lifts German DAX to record high.
newsitem.headline: Wall Street cheer lifts German DAX to record high.

text.p: Fresh demand for car shares and delight at Wall Street's strong gains on Friday lifted Germany's blue chip DAX share index to record highs on Monday.
The 30-share DAX vaulted past old records at its opening to trade up 64.40 points, or, 1.9 percent at 3,524.71 points in early bourse trade.
Part of its surge was a simple catch-up from Friday afternoon, when prices advanced strongly in the late post-bourse session following the release of well-received U.S. economic data.
"Things are fairly much booming," said a Frankfurt dealer, who warned, however, that turnover was likely to be thin because of the U.K. market holiday today.
"But we can be very happy if we close above 3,500 (DAX points)," he said.
Dollar-sensitive car shares led the advance, with Volkswagen AG up 4.2 percent at 1,206 marks in early trade and Daimler-Benz up four percent at 137 marks.
Financial shares were also firmly ahead, with index heavyweight Allianz AG Holding up 3.4 percent at 345.50 marks.

The underperformer of the day was software company SAP AG, whose DAX-listed preferred stock fell two percent to 314 marks after Frankfurt prosecutors said they were probing a potentially serious insider trading case involving the company.
Dealers downplayed the move, noting that SAP is notoriously volatile.
"This (the story) is mainly a negative from a sentiment point of view," said a dealer. "It makes no difference to fundamentals."

Chemicals giant Hoechst was also under pressure, trading down 65 pfennigs at 67 marks, after reporting first-quarter pretax profit of 831 million marks, slightly below many estimated, according to dealers.

"Overall the numbers were slightly disappointing," said Christian Faitz, chemicals analyst at Trinkaus Capital Management, who noted that the data had been hard to predict because of Hoechst's current phase of restructuring.
